063e4a112f59b2c8938e: The cost of building a WordPress website: what can you expect? WordPress is a flexible and free content management system (CMS), which allows anyone to set up a website. It operates over 40% of the websites on the Internet, thanks to its ability to adapt to any purpose - from simple image websites to complex virtual stores. So how much does it cost to build a WordPress website? It is important to remember that although the system itself is free, building a professional website involves various costs. The final price varies depending on a number of factors, so it is important to understand them before starting: Type of website: image website (usually cheaper) versus a virtual store with a clearing system (more expensive). Complexity and functionality: number of pages, need for special plugins, order systems, forums and more. Development and design services: will you build the website yourself or will you need a professional designer and developer? Website content: Will you write the content yourself or hire a professional copywriter? Building a WordPress site can start with just a few hundred shekels for a basic site, and reach tens of thousands of shekels for particularly complex sites. Most of the business websites are in the range of NIS 3,000 to NIS 15,000. Details of the costs of building a WordPress site As we mentioned, the total cost of building a WordPress site consists of several main factors. To get a more complete picture, it is important to know all the actions and costs involved in the process: Domain registration: This is the first step on the way to building the website. The domain is your website address (for example: www.yoursite.co.il). Its cost ranges from 50 to 150 NIS per year, and depends on the type of domain and the provider. Website hosting (Hosting): Once you have a domain, you will need to store the website on a dedicated server. Quality hosting is essential for the website's speed and reliability. The prices for WordPress hosting packages start at around 20 NIS per month and can vary depending on the size of the site and the expected traffic. Design kit (Theme): The design kit is the visual basis of the site. You can choose from thousands of free design kits, or purchase a professional kit that will give a unique and modern look. The cost of a paid design kit ranges from 50 NIS to a few hundred shekels, and is usually a one-time purchase. Content development and writing: quality content is the engine of the site. The cost of professional writing can range from 500 to 1,500 NIS per page, and varies according to the complexity of the content and the expertise required. If you choose to write the content yourself, you can save on this cost, but it is important to invest a lot of time so that the content is high-quality, relevant and friendly to search engines. Building Landing Pages: Landing pages are intended for specific marketing purposes, such as campaigns and advertising. Page development cost Professional landing usually starts at NIS 500 per page and varies according to the complexity and required features. Development of plugins and custom applications: WordPress allows you to expand its functionality through plugins. For unique needs that do not exist in the free or paid plugins, you may be required to develop a custom plugin. The cost here can vary in a very wide range and depends on the nature of the development. How much does it cost to build a WordPress website? Advantages of building a website on WordPress As we have seen, WordPress is a very popular choice, and there are several main reasons for this. The platform offers notable advantages, especially for small and medium-sized businesses, which make it one of the leading options on the market: Low cost: One of the most prominent advantages of WordPress is that it allows you to build a high-quality and relatively advanced website at a low cost. The platform itself is free, and the main costs come from domain, storage and design. Additionally, availability of thousands of free plugins and theme kits helps keep costs down. Large and supportive community: WordPress has a huge and active global community of developers, designers and users. This means that you can always find support, training, updates, and experts who can help you with any problem or need. Plugins: Plugins allow you to add special functionality to the website (such as contact forms, galleries or security). From the advertising revolution: from the "golden marketing" of the past to the "Google marketing" of today, have you ever asked yourself how they advertised before the Internet? Businesses have invested a lot of money in advertising on television, radio, newspapers and billboards. It was "expensive marketing" - difficult to measure its impact. You could spend millions on a TV campaign, but you didn't really know how many people saw the ad or how many people came into business because of it. It was a gamble! Only the big businesses could afford it. Then, in the late 90s and early 2000s, a big change came to the world of marketing: the Internet and Google. Suddenly, people could search for information and products at the click of a button. Google quickly realized the great potential of this instant desire and created a new platform called Google AdWords (today Google Ads), which changed the rules of the game. Google Ads: advertising for everyone Since then, every business, even the smallest, can appear at the top of the search results. Not only the big businesses and the "rich" can advertise, but with an advertising method for everyone. The pay-per-click (PPC) model means that you only pay if someone is interested who searched for your product or service and actually clicks on your ad. And that's the big change! Suddenly with this model you can measure everything, know how much you spent on advertising and how much revenue it brought. The ability to target ads to a specific audience (by keywords, location, etc.) and control over the budget made advertising efficient and economical. Since then, Google has not stopped innovating. The system has evolved and now, in 2025, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) has turned it into a powerful and smart marketing tool. It is not just a search engine, but an answer engine that understands the user's intent in a better way. Google advertising campaign: what is it anyway? The term "campaign" may seem complicated, but actually a Google campaign is a sequence of settings, ads and budget designed to achieve a specific business goal. It could be: bringing leads (potential customers) to your business. Increasing sales directly on the website. Building brand awareness and exposure to a wide audience. Increasing traffic to the website or physical store. The advantage of Google Ads is its ability to reach customers when they are looking for what you offer, at the right place and time - from search results to YouTube videos. Today, in 2025, the AI ​​does this work for you. Main types of Google campaigns in the age of AI (2025 and beyond) Choosing the right campaign type is essential, and it also includes thinking about Google's automation: Search Network Campaigns: "The money is in the customer's pocket - let the AI ​​find it!" what is this These are the ads that appear at the top of Google's search results. When a customer types "computer repair in Ramat Gan" or "vegan catering for events", your ad can appear immediately. The innovation in 2025: most ads are responsive search ads (RSA - Responsive Search Ads). You enter a number of titles and descriptions, and Google's AI puts together the winning combination appropriate for each search. That way your ad will always be relevant. The big advantage: this is advertising with a high purchase intent. People who are actively searching are more likely to buy from you, and even the AI ​​shortens the process and ensures that your message is accurate. 2. Display Network Campaigns: "To be everywhere - but in a smart and visual way!" what is this These are the visual ads (banners, images, and sometimes a short video) that appear on thousands of websites and partner Google apps. Imagine digital billboards, but much more focused. The innovation in 2025: here, too, most ads are responsive media network ads (RDA - Responsive Display Ads). You provide Google with some assets (images, logos, titles), and the AI ​​displays the ad in the most appropriate way for each location and screen size. How does it function? Audiences can be targeted in sophisticated ways, such as: personalized audiences, lookalike audiences, and smart remarketing. If someone has visited your site, the AI ​​will show them your ads when they are on other sites. The big advantage: wide exposure, building brand awareness, and the ability to reach potential customers who already know you. 3. Video Campaigns: "A picture is worth a thousand words, a video is worth a million - and AI helps!" what is this Video ads that appear on YouTube and sometimes also on partner sites. The innovation in 2025: video campaigns are more targeted, and AI helps to know when the audience is watching the video. Emphasis on short formats that are easy to watch. The big advantage: a strong visual feeling and from Amazing the story in front of the audience, while being exposed to a wide audience. 4. Google Shopping Campaigns: "When you see the product - you want to buy, and the AI ​​presents it perfectly!" what is this If you sell physical products (ecommerce store), this campaign is for you! The ads show a picture of the product, the price and the name of the store at the top of the search results. The innovation in 2025: shopping campaigns that are much more visual and targeted by the AI. Google presents your products in the best possible way, including a direct shopping experience from Google. The big advantage: great exposure to your products and very high conversion rates. 5. Performance Max (PMax): "The campaign that drives the AI ​​powerfully - all together!" what is this The most innovative type of campaign in Google Ads, will probably be dominant in 2025. The PMax campaign allows you to reach your audiences on all Google channels: search, media, YouTube and more - all from one campaign! how does it work You provide PMax with your business objectives and your assets. The AI ​​uses machine learning to find the best combinations and show the ads to the right audiences, on all channels and at the optimal times. The big advantage: simple management (everything in one place), maximizing potential in all channels, and automatic optimization that results in improved performance. 61503c9ea7a982c055db: Google Shopping - the essential tool for growing your sales site Find out how to advertise your products on Google Shopping and use the tool to promote sales, leads and website traffic. Online shopping - we all do it! And it is without a doubt the biggest thing in the last decade. Online shopping has long been an integral part of our lives. If you have an online store, you surely aim to increase exposure, attract more potential customers and increase sales. One of the most effective ways to achieve this is through Google Shopping. Sales shop owner? Want more exposure, more sales? Promote your store and products in the most prominent position on Google. Promotion on Google Shopping is a must-have tool for you! Have you ever looked for a specific product and found yourself jumping between countless websites, comparing prices and features? The process can be exhausting. This is where services that centralize products from a variety of stores in one place come into play. While marketplace sites such as Amazon, eBay and others play an important role, Google Shopping offers a unique and central platform directly within the world's largest search engine. Google Shopping allows potential buyers to discover, compare and buy products from a wide variety of sellers, all from the familiar Google search experience. For you, as a seller, this means tremendous exposure to a target audience that is actively looking for what you offer. Clicking on your product leads the buyer directly to your website to complete the purchase - this sponsored advertising transformation makes the platform a powerful engine for driving quality traffic and sales. If you're not taking advantage of Google Shopping, you're probably missing out on a significant opportunity. This guide is designed to help you deeply understand the platform, its benefits and how you can start leveraging it for your business in 2025. A shopping campaign is profitable for both buyers and sellers (advertisers) and is considered one of the most effective ways to advertise products on Google these days. Google Shopping is: Powerful: Google Shopping applies Google's search technology to help you find and research products from online stores around the web and then directs you directly to where you can buy them. Comprehensive: Find everything from common to unusual products. Fast: Almost immediately after entering a search, you'll see images of relevant products and links to more information, including the stores that sell them. What is Google Shopping? Google Shopping is a service from Google that allows consumers to search, compare and discover physical products offered for sale by retailers and sellers across the Internet. The service functions as a price comparison engine (CSE - Comparison Shopping Engine) and displays rich visual search results. The history of the service begins in 2002 under the name "Froogle", which acted as a product index. In 2012, Google made a significant change and turned the service into a paid advertising model (Pay-Per-Click), where retailers have to pay for their products to appear in prominent positions. Today, Google Shopping is an integral part of the Google Ads advertising platform. It is important to distinguish between two main components in Google Shopping: Shopping Ads: These are paid ads (PPC) that appear in prominent positions in Google's search results, in the dedicated "Shopping" tab, in Google Photos, on Google's partner sites, and sometimes also on YouTube, Discover and Gmail (mainly through Performance Max campaigns). The ads are activated and managed through the Google Ads account and are based on product data uploaded to Google Merchant Center. Free Product Listings: Google also allows an organic (free) presentation of products, mainly in the "Shopping" tab, but sometimes also in the main search results and in Google Images. To appear for free, a Google Merchant Center account and a valid product feed are still required, but there is no cost for clicks. Unlike regular Google text ads that are based on targeting keywords that the advertiser chooses, Shopping ads (and the free tickets) rely on a Product Feed. This feed contains detailed information about each product you sell (name, description, price, image, brand, availability, etc.). Google scans the feed and uses this information to automatically match the relevant products to the users' search queries. Why should you use shopping ads on Google? Most online shopping trips start with a Google search. A strong Google Shopping presence is critical to reaching potential customers at the exact moment they are looking for the products you offer. Here are some key reasons why this is a must-have tool: Prominent visual visibility: Shopping ads often appear at the top of search results, above text ads and organic results, or in a prominent position alongside them. The visual format (image, price, familiar name) catches the eye and provides critical information at a glance, leading to higher click-through rates (CTR) compared to text ads for product queries. Quality and targeted traffic: a user who clicks on a shopping ad has already seen the product image, its price and the name of the seller. Therefore, these clicks tend to be of higher quality, with a higher probability of leading to a purchase, because the user arrives at the product page with clear expectations. Wider exposure: Your products can appear in a variety of locations on the Google network (search, shopping, images, YouTube, partners, etc.), and in addition, several of your shopping ads or a shopping ad and your text ad can appear together for the same search query, which increases your "real estate" on the results page. Competitive advantage: if your competitors use Google Shopping and you don't, you lose significant market share. Presence on the platform allows you to compete directly and display your benefits (price, promotions, availability). Google Ads provides detailed tools for tracking the performance of shopping ads, including impressions, costs, and return on advertising expenses (ROAS). Free exposure: In addition to paid ads, the opportunity to appear in free product cards provides additional exposure and traffic Shopping ads are visible and usually contain: Product name (headline): Current product price: Your brand or store name, special offers (like "free shipping"), or local availability: Google's main search results page (google.com): Usually appears as a carousel of images at the top of the page, or in a separate column (usually on the right side on desktop computers) Can appear alongside text ads and organic results. The "Shopping Tab": a dedicated tab within the Google search engine, which only displays product results (ads and free tickets) and enables more advanced filtering and comparison. Google Images: Relevant shopping ads can appear when users search for images related to products. Google search network partner sites: If you have selected this option in the campaign settings, ads can also appear on other sites that use the Google search engine. YouTube, Discover, Gmail: Mainly through automated smart campaigns like Performance Max, Google can present your products to relevant audiences on these platforms as well. It's important to note that both paid ads and free tickets can appear at the same time, with the paid ads usually getting more prominent placements. How does Google Shopping work? The field of search engine optimization (AEO) has been gaining popularity in recent years, causing many to wonder: what is AEO? Is this the end of the road for traditional SEO? Will answer engines make traditional search engines obsolete? The short answer is - no. Although AEO is a significant development in the digital world, it does not replace traditional SEO. In fact, AEO offers a significant boost to SEO strategies, and improves user experience and visibility in search results. In this article, we'll look at the differences between AEO and SEO, how they fit together, and how you can upgrade your digital marketing strategy to get the most out of both tools. What is an AEO? How is it different from SEO? AEO, or Answer Engine Optimization, is a new approach to search engines that focuses on providing direct and accurate answers to users' questions. Unlike traditional search engines that direct you to different websites and pages that contain information, AEO offers a direct and focused answer within the search results, usually in the form of a featured snippet. The goal is to provide the most accurate answer to the question, without the user having to go to additional websites. For example, if you search for a question like "What is the AEO?", the search engine can display a direct answer that summarizes the information from your website. On the other hand, SEO (search engine optimization) focuses on improving the ways of accessing websites, so that the search engines know how to present your website in the search results based on criteria such as keyword relevance, content quality, external links and more. Will AEO replace SEO? Although AEO (answer engine optimization) is gaining popularity and becoming an important trend in digital marketing, it is not expected to replace traditional SEO. Instead, AEO joins as an additional element designed to enhance and complement existing SEO strategies. Search engines still rely on traditional factors such as content quality, site structure and external links to determine rankings. AEO works alongside this, while improving the user experience and optimizing content in a way that directly answers the surfer's questions, thus being able to appear more in immediate answers and featured content sections. AEO and SEO work together to increase digital visibility and provide an optimal user experience. How do AEO and SEO fit together? The understanding that AEO and SEO do not replace each other, but are combined together, allows you to get the most out of both tools and achieve optimal results. In fact, the two work in a complementary way and include the following reasons: SEO remains the foundation - search engines still rely on traditional SEO factors, such as keywords, site structure and link quality, to determine rankings. AEO upgrades SEO – AEO bases itself on the foundation of SEO and promotes the content to appear more prominently in the search results, including displaying direct answers to the surfer's questions. Improving the user experience - AEO provides direct answers, which increases the user experience and reduces the rate of leaving the page (Bounce Rate), thereby also contributing to the website's visibility in search engines. Cooperation to improve visibility – AEO and SEO work together to improve the overall visibility of the site, in that SEO ensures that the content appears in search results, and AEO helps it stand out and be more available in narrow search data. Through a perfect combination of AEO and SEO, you can maximize digital results and achieve higher exposure, improvement in search results and increased conversions. Optimizing for Voice Searches Also, increasing use of voice assistants like Google Assistant and Siri requires adapting your content for voice searches. You must ensure that your answers are clear, direct and use natural language in question. 4. Using Structured Data Use Schema Markup to help search engines better understand your content and increase your chances of appearing in featured sections or rich results. 5. Optimizing for Instant Answers One of the most effective methods to appear in AEO results is to create content focused on providing instant answers. ffabe41242716d1411fa: Remarketing Guide (Remarketing) Remarketing, also known as remarketing, is a smart strategy used by business owners to return to surfers who have already visited their site. It is an advertising tool that allows you to remind visitors of the products or services they were interested in, thus motivating them to come back and make a purchase. In this article, we will explain in a simple and clear way what remarketing is, why it is essential to the success of your business, and what steps can be taken to leverage it effectively through platforms such as Google and social networks. With these techniques, you can increase your website's conversion rate and gain higher visibility among your potential audience. What is remarketing? Remarketing is an advertising strategy that allows you to show targeted ads to users who have visited your website or used your app. The technology is based on "cookies" - small tracking files that identify specific users and allow advertisers to show them customized ads on other websites, on social networks like Facebook and Instagram, and on search engines like Google. For example, if someone visited your site and saw a certain product, but didn't complete a purchase, you could show them an ad that reminds them of that product or offers them a discount, hoping to get them to come back to the site and complete the purchase. Why is remarketing important? The main benefit of remarketing is the ability to reach a targeted audience that has already shown interest in your business, increasing the chance of converting them into customers. Here are some main reasons why you should integrate remarketing into your marketing strategy: Increasing conversions: Most surfers tend to leave the site without making a purchase or leaving details. Remarketing allows you to remind them of what they were interested in and get them to come back and take the action. Strengthening the brand: repeated exposure to your ads on social networks, search engines or other websites strengthens your brand awareness. The more visitors are exposed to your brand, the more likely they will remember it and treat it as a trusted and familiar source. Advanced segmentation: Remarketing allows you to segment your audience according to their behavior on the site. For example, you can show ads to those who visited a certain product page, to those who added products to the cart but did not complete a purchase, or to those who viewed certain content and did not continue. When surfers visit your website, their browser receives a cookie, which is a small piece of information that is saved on the user's device and is used to track their actions on the Internet. These cookies allow advertisers to identify the surfers and examine their behavior on your site, such as pages they visited, products they viewed, or actions that were not completed, such as a purchase or subscription to a newsletter. With the help of tools like Google Ads and Facebook Pixel, you can collect important data about your website visitors. A Facebook Pixel, for example, is a code that is inserted into your website and allows you to track the actions of users after visiting the website, which helps to tailor ads to users according to their behavior. As soon as the users leave your website, the system recognizes the users with the help of the cookies and allows them to display personalized ads in other places around the Internet. Whether it is advertising on Google, Facebook, or other platforms, this process helps you bring back the surfers and increase the chance that they will return to your site and perform the desired action, such as a purchase or leaving details. In this way, remarketing not only helps focus your marketing efforts, but also creates an improved user experience, as the ads you show are more relevant to people who have already shown interest in your products or services. Can this supplier be trusted?… and the list goes on and on. And the reviews can actually answer almost all of them. Companies spend millions on marketing and advertising every year. But at the end of the day, the opinions of other customers are worth more. Online reviews can help you make up your mind as well as potential customers looking for your service or product. And it doesn't matter if you are looking for a restaurant to have lunch, a hotel, a locksmith, a recommended technician, a new computer, a mobile phone, the best coffee machine or anything else... Negative reviews and recommendations (G2): You will find it hard to believe but negative reviews can work in your favor! 72% of buyers say that negative reviews give depth and insight into a product. 40% of buyers say that negative reviews help build credibility for the product. 82% of buyers specifically look for negative reviews.
